# Problem setup:

## Points

- A(-2.0081, -1.4301)
- B(0.2739, -0.4604)
- C(0.0976, -1.9013)
- E(-0.6800, -1.7273)
- M(-0.9181, -0.9669)
- N(0.2415, -0.7257)
- O(-0.8192, -1.0579)

## Assumptions:

[C0] : EN = AE
[C1] : EM = CE
[C2] : AM = MN
[C3] : ∠(BM,BN) = 1pi/3
[C4] : CN = MN
[C5] : AN ⟂ EM
[C6] : CM ⟂ EN

## Numerical checks

[N0] : A, E, N are not collinear
[N1] : C, E, M are not collinear
[N2] : A, M, N are not collinear
[N3] : C, M, N are not collinear


# Goals

A, N, O are collinear : Proved [14]
C, M, O are collinear : Proved [16]


# Proof:

000. | EN = AE [C0], A, E, N are not collinear [N0] =(r13 Isosceles triangle equal angles)> ∠(AE,AN) = ∠(AN,EN) [0]
001. | EM = CE [C1], C, E, M are not collinear [N1] =(r13 Isosceles triangle equal angles)> ∠(CE,CM) = ∠(CM,EM) [1]
002. | ∠(AE,AN) = ∠(AN,EN) [0], ∠(CE,CM) = ∠(CM,EM) [1] =(AR Deduction)> AE ∥ CE [2]
003. | AE ∥ CE [2] =(r28 Overlapping parallels)> A, C, E are collinear [3]
004. | A, C, E are collinear [3] =(r82 Parallel from collinear)> AC ∥ AE [4]
005. | AM = MN [C2], A, M, N are not collinear [N2] =(r13 Isosceles triangle equal angles)> ∠(AM,AN) = ∠(AN,MN) [5]
006. | ∠(AM,AN) = ∠(AN,MN) [5] =(AR Deduction)> AM ∥ BM [6]
007. | AM ∥ BM [6] =(r28 Overlapping parallels)> A, B, M are collinear [7]
008. | A, B, M are collinear [7] =(r82 Parallel from collinear)> AM ∥ AB [8]
009. | CN = MN [C4], C, M, N are not collinear [N3] =(r13 Isosceles triangle equal angles)> ∠(CM,CN) = ∠(MN,CM) [9]
010. | ∠(BM,BN) = 1pi/3 [C3], ∠(CM,CN) = ∠(MN,CM) [9] =(AR Deduction)> CN ∥ BN [10]
011. | CN ∥ BN [10] =(r28 Overlapping parallels)> B, C, N are collinear [11]
012. | B, C, N are collinear [11] =(r82 Parallel from collinear)> BN ∥ BC [12]
013. | AC ∥ AE [4], AM ∥ AB [8], BN ∥ BC [12], AN ⟂ EM [C5] =(AR Deduction)> AN ∥ AO [13]
014. | AN ∥ AO [13] =(r28 Overlapping parallels)> A, N, O are collinear [14]
015. | AC ∥ AE [4], BN ∥ BC [12], CM ⟂ EN [C6] =(AR Deduction)> CO ∥ CM [15]
016. | CO ∥ CM [15] =(r28 Overlapping parallels)> C, M, O are collinear [16]


# Appendix: AR deductions:



002. | Angle Chasing to prove AE ∥ CE:
| Premise ∠(AE,AN) = ∠(AN,EN) gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise ∠(CE,CM) = ∠(CM,EM) gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
We are left with a linear equation with coefficients {} that gives AE ∥ CE



006. | Angle Chasing to prove AM ∥ BM:
| Premise ∠(AM,AN) = ∠(AN,MN) gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
We are left with a linear equation with coefficients {} that gives AM ∥ BM



010. | Angle Chasing to prove CN ∥ BN:
| Premise ∠(BM,BN) = 1pi/3 gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise ∠(CM,CN) = ∠(MN,CM) gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
We are left with a linear equation with coefficients {} that gives CN ∥ BN



013. | Angle Chasing to prove AN ∥ AO:
| Premise AC ∥ AE gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise AM ∥ AB gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise BN ∥ BC gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise AN ⟂ EM gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
We are left with a linear equation with coefficients {} that gives AN ∥ AO



015. | Angle Chasing to prove CO ∥ CM:
| Premise AC ∥ AE gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise BN ∥ BC gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise CM ⟂ EN gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
We are left with a linear equation with coefficients {} that gives CO ∥ CM

End of proof.
